html:
1The exam at a glance

The Practitioner exam does not test whether you can recall the method. It tests whether you can apply it to a project scenario and analyze whether an action is appropriate.

Item Fact
Book Open book: the Official Book, which you may annotate; no other material
Time 150 minutes; 188 minutes if the exam is not in your native or working language
Marks 70 marks, 1 mark per part question, no negative marking
Pass mark 42 of 70 (60%)
Thinking Bloom 3 (apply to a situation) and Bloom 4 (analyze whether an action is effective)
Format A Project Scenario, Additional Information about people, and the questions

The Additional Information describes people who work on the project. At least one question needs it, so read it every time a question names a person.

Question type What you see Marks
Classic A short situation, a question and four options A to D; often "Was this an appropriate action, and why?" with two "Yes, because" and two "No, because" options 1 mark
Matching Three pieces of information and a list of five or six options; match each piece to one option; an option may be used once, more than once or not at all 3 marks, one for each part

Each of the three parts is marked on its own, so a partly right matching answer still earns marks.

Exam tip

. In a classic question, decide yes or no first, then choose the reason. Two options share your decision; only one of them gives a reason that fits the facts in the scenario.

2The four learning outcomes and their weights

Learning outcome Weight About (of 70 marks) Modules
1. Principles in context 10% 7 1
2. People management 9% 6 2
3. Practices in context 51% 36 3 to 9
4. Processes in context 30% 21 10 to 16

Each practice and each process has two criteria:

  • Apply (Bloom 3): the management products, the areas of focus of the key roles, and effective management and techniques (practices); or the activities, inputs, outputs and roles (processes).
  • Analyze (Bloom 4): is the approach effective and fit for purpose, considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring? This is the harder kind.
Exam tip

. The seven practices are 51% of the marks, and with the processes you reach 81%. Put most of your study time there.

3Pass strategy and the open book

150 minutes for 70 marks is a little over 2 minutes per mark (about 2.7 with 188 minutes). A matching question has three marks, so give it about 5 minutes.

Rule How
First pass Answer every classic question you can in about 2 minutes
Mark and return If a question needs over 3 minutes, choose the best option, mark it and move on
Reserve time Keep about 15 minutes at the end for marked questions
Never leave a blank There is no negative marking, so a guess costs nothing
Pass arithmetic 42 of 70 lets you miss 28 part questions

How to use the open book:

Habit Why
Annotate Write short cues beside each practice's roles table, product list and tailoring section
Tab Mark every principle, people, practice and process section and each roles table
Know where things are Practice finding any table in under 30 seconds
Do not rely on reading A chapter takes minutes you do not have; the book confirms a detail
Check the rules Read PeopleCert's current candidate rules on what may be added to the book
Exam tip

. Use the book to confirm, not to learn. If you must read a whole section to understand a question, mark it and move on.

4The five-step method for a classic question

  1. Read the scenario and the last line. Note the stage, the names, the numbers and any tolerance. If a person is named, check the Additional Information.
  2. Find the process or practice. Which process is the project in, and which practice owns the topic?
  3. Check roles and authority. Who may decide, who approves, who must only be told?
  4. Check tolerances and principles. Inside tolerance the project manager acts; a forecast breach goes up. Does the action break a principle?
  5. Choose the option whose reason is right, not only whose action is right. Two options often share the right action and differ in the reason.

Worked example. In the build stage of Project Harbor, Sam Okafor forecasts a cost overrun of 3 percent against a stage tolerance of plus or minus 10 percent. He deals with it inside the stage and notes it in the next highlight report. Was this appropriate?

Step 2: controlling a stage. Step 3: the project manager has the authority. Step 4: inside tolerance, so manage by exception. Step 5: "Yes, because it is within tolerance and so within delegated authority."

For a matching question, apply the method to each part separately. Options can be reused, so never cross one off after using it.

Exam tip

. The reason decides the mark. If two options both say "Yes", compare the "because" clauses with the scenario facts and the role's authority.

5Project Harbor and a study plan

Scenarios in this course use one fictional project.

Item Fact
Project Brightwater Port Authority replaces its paper berth-permit process with an online permit service
Budget and time 480,000 and nine months
Stages Initiation, build, pilot, rollout
Board Marta Quinn, executive (director of operations); Tomas Reyes, senior user (harbor master); Lena Kovac, senior supplier (account director, Delta Software)
Management Sam Okafor, project manager; Wei Chen, team manager (Delta Software's developers)
Support roles Aisha Bello, project assurance (finance business partner); Jon Park, project support; Tomas Reyes also has the delegated authority for small changes
Tolerances Typically plus or minus 10 percent cost and plus or minus two weeks time per stage

A six-week plan:

Week Modules Focus
1 0 to 2 Exam method, principles, people
2 3 to 5 Business case, organization, plans
3 6 to 9 Quality, risk, issues, progress
4 10 to 13 Starting up, directing, initiating, controlling a stage
5 14 to 16 Managing product delivery, stage boundary, closing
6 17 Timed practice, weak spots, book tabs

For each module: read the note, read the matching Official Book pages (roles table, products, tailoring), annotate them, then answer the questions with the book closed and check every miss.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A candidate in the 150-minute exam spends 6 minutes on one classic question, then picks the better option, marks it and moves on. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because a marked best guess saves time for other questions
  • BYes, because a marked question is scored as half a mark later
  • CNo, because every question must be fully resolved before the next
  • DNo, because a wrong guess loses a mark through negative marking
Show the answer

Answer: A. The method is to mark and return, and since there is no negative marking a best guess costs nothing while the time saved earns marks elsewhere.

S2In a matching question on Project Harbor, a candidate matches part 1 to the senior user, crosses that role off, and so cannot use it for part 2, which also fits. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because each option can be used only once in a matching question
  • BYes, because a role is responsible for one action in each question
  • CNo, because every option in the list must be used at least once
  • DNo, because options may be used once, more than once or not at all
Show the answer

Answer: D. Matching options can be reused or left unused, so crossing one off throws away a correct answer.

S3During preparation a candidate writes short cues beside the roles table of each practice in the Official Book, so each table can be found in seconds. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because the exam rewards reading long sections during the sitting
  • BYes, because the book may be annotated and quick lookup saves time
  • CNo, because an annotated book may not be taken into the exam
  • DNo, because the exam tests recall and the book will not be needed
Show the answer

Answer: B. The open-book rule allows notes inside the book, and fast lookup helps confirm a detail without reading whole chapters.

S4A candidate has six weeks and wants study time to follow the marks. Which plan fits the weights best?

  • AEqual time on principles, people, practices and processes alike
  • BMost time on the processes, because they cover the whole project life
  • CMost time on practices, then processes, then principles and people
  • DMost time on principles and people, because they apply everywhere
Show the answer

Answer: C. Practices carry 51% and processes 30%, so they should take most of the time, while principles are 10% and people 9%.

S5A question asks how Sam Okafor should tell Lena Kovac about a delay. Where should the candidate look for her communication preferences?

  • AIn the Additional Information about the people on the project
  • BIn the Official Book's role description for the senior supplier
  • CIn the stage plan that the Project Scenario gives for the pilot
  • DIn the answer options, which always repeat these preferences
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Additional Information gives facts about named people, and at least one question depends on it.

S6A candidate leaves one part of a matching question blank to avoid losing a mark. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because a wrong answer in one part cancels a correct part
  • BYes, because matching is scored only when all three parts are right
  • CNo, because wrong answers cost nothing and each part earns a mark
  • DNo, because a blank part makes the other two parts score zero
Show the answer

Answer: C. Each part is a one-mark part question and wrong answers cost nothing, so a blank can only lose marks.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the pass mark?

Show the answer

42 of 70 marks (60%).

R2How long is the exam, and how long with extra time?

Show the answer

150 minutes; 188 minutes if the exam is not in your native or working language.

R3What are the weights of the four learning outcomes?

Show the answer

Principles 10%, people 9%, practices 51% and processes 30%.

R4Which Bloom levels does the exam use?

Show the answer

Level 3 (apply) and level 4 (analyze).

R5How many marks is a matching question worth, and may options repeat?

Show the answer

Three marks, one per part; options may be used once, more than once or not at all.

R6What is the fifth step of the method for a classic question?

Show the answer

Choose the option whose reason is right, not only whose action is right.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Format open book (the Official Book, annotated); 150 minutes, 188 with extra time; 70 marks; pass 42
Thinking Bloom 3 apply and Bloom 4 analyze, on a scenario with Additional Information about people
Question types classic (1 mark, four options) and matching (3 marks, reusable options)
Weights principles 10%, people 9%, practices 51%, processes 30%
Time about 2 minutes per mark; mark and return; keep 15 minutes; never leave a blank
Open book annotate, tab, know the tables; confirm, do not learn
Method scenario, process or practice, roles and authority, tolerances and principles, right reason
